state.user_request_16_nov: 8.12 shall have if_revision. Jev and Laya agree design and acceptance first. The row: if_revision, idempotency keys, batch-as-one-undo. Done when: a retry after a timeout does not duplicate. ADR-0002 D.1 principle 4: every write takes if_revision and returns the new revision; a batch is one transaction and one undo entry. ADR D.4: idempotency keys on writes so a retried call after a timeout does not duplicate an object. The plan reopens 8.12 until the editor MCP edit path takes both through gx-write-semantics and the retry-after-timeout test runs against that path.
facts: gx-write-semantics (Shared/write-semantics) already has guarded(current, if_revision) -> next revision or RevisionMismatch{expected, actual}, a bounded IdempotencyLedger with once(key, operation), and a Batch type. No crate depends on it.

Every MCP write is CommandTool

: it parses the tool payload strictly, builds a fresh Workspace over the on-disk project store, runs Workspace::execute and returns the outcome. The MCP server process holds no state between calls. A stdio MCP server is started per client session, so a client that times out and reconnects can reach a new process.

scenes.edit with a Stored target does read_scene, apply_edits, then write_scene (an atomic file replace) only when the document changed; there is no lock, so two writers can both read revision N and the last one silently wins. The Editor shell's Save of a session opened from a stored scene also calls write_scene and overwrites whatever is stored.

SceneDocument.revision is Option<Revision>, documented as the monotonic authoring revision and the optimistic-concurrency token (0.8). Nothing ever increments it. The content hash leaves it out. Publishing pins a clone to Revision(1) if absent and the engine issues its own Take revision, so the published Take revision is a different counter owned by Playout.
A batch (EditScene.edits) is already atomic and one undo entry in a session; against a stored scene it is applied to one in-memory copy and written once, so it lands whole or not at all.
Refusal::RevisionMismatch {expected, actual} already exists with the code revisionMismatch; Revision::check_write is the one comparison.

scenes.create refuses an existing id and scenes.import refuses an existing id, so a retried create after a lost reply is refused by name rather than duplicated; scenes.delete of an absent scene is reported, never treated as success.
state.proposal: Token: SceneDocument.revision, absent read as 0, bumped by exactly 1 on every stored write by any writer (MCP edit, Editor Save to origin). EditScene and DeleteScene gain if_revision; a Stored target must carry it, a Session target must not. The write is read-check-write under a per-store lock so the check and the write are one step; a stale write is refused revisionMismatch with the current revision, nothing written. Every MCP write also takes an optional idempotency key; the server records the key, a hash of the tool and arguments, and the first result in a bounded durable ledger in the project store, returns the first result for a repeat with the same arguments, and refuses a repeat with different arguments by name. The result of scenes.edit, scenes.create and scenes.delete carries the new revision.

token.instructions: What should if_revision compare against for a stored scene?

criteria.authoring_revision: SceneDocument.revision, bumped by one on every stored write by any writer; absent reads as 0.
criteria.separate_counter: A new edit counter kept beside the scene in the project store, leaving SceneDocument.revision for publishing.
criteria.published_revision: The published Take revision that Cue and Take pin.

required.instructions: Must a write to a stored scene carry if_revision?

criteria.required_on_stored: Required for a Stored target: a missing if_revision is refused by name, so no agent overwrites blind by omission.
criteria.optional_last_write_wins: Optional: when omitted the write is unconditional.

where_it_lives.instructions: Where should the revision check and bump live?

criteria.in_the_store_write: In the Editor's stored-scene write path, called by the command executor, so the MCP edit and the Editor's own save share one rule and one lock.
criteria.mcp_wrapper_only: In the MCP tool wrapper only; the Editor's own writes stay unguarded.
criteria.two_copies: Implement the check in the MCP wrapper and again in the Editor.

editor_save.instructions: What should the Editor's Save of a session opened from a stored scene do?

criteria.check_and_bump: Refuse with revisionMismatch if the stored scene moved on since the session read it, and bump the revision when it saves.
criteria.bump_only: Always overwrite but bump the revision, so agents notice.
criteria.unchanged: Leave Save as it is: last write wins and the revision is not touched.

ledger.instructions: Where should the idempotency ledger live?

criteria.durable_in_project_store: A bounded file in the project store, written atomically, so a retry that reaches a restarted or second server process still gets the first result.
criteria.in_memory_per_process: In the MCP server process memory, lost when the process restarts.

key_reuse.instructions: What should a repeated idempotency key with different arguments do?

criteria.refuse_by_name: Refuse with a named refusal; the key belongs to the first request.
criteria.return_first_result: Return the first result regardless of the new arguments.
criteria.execute_again: Treat it as a new write.

crash_window.instructions: A write can land and the process die before the ledger records it. Which makes a retry safe?

criteria.revision_guard_covers_it: The retried edit carries the same if_revision, which is now stale, so it is refused revisionMismatch and never applied twice; creates refuse an existing id.
criteria.ledger_must_be_in_the_same_file: Only storing the key inside the scene file itself makes it safe.

which_tools.instructions: Which MCP writes take which guard?

criteria.revision_on_edit_and_delete_key_on_all: scenes.edit and scenes.delete take if_revision; every write tool takes an idempotency key; creates have no revision to check.
criteria.revision_on_all: Every write takes if_revision, including creates.

needs_user.instructions: Must the user approve this design before implementation?

criteria.true: Yes, it makes a product choice the recorded user decisions do not cover.
criteria.false: No, it follows from ADR-0002 D.1 and D.4, the plan's reopening condition and the user's instruction that 8.12 shall have if_revision.
